newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to cut number of international airports.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to cut number of international airports.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has ordered a cut in the number of airports serving international routes because it cannot afford to pay customs and passport control officers, a government spokesman said on Monday.

Aviation sources said seven airports will have their rights to serve international flights removed, including airports at the regional centres of Vinnytsya, Khmelnitsky and Cherkassy in the centre of the country.

The spokesman said 16 of 36 airports, as well as one cargo airfield in the town of Hostomel near Kiev, are currently authorised by the Transport Ministry's Aviation Department to serve international flights.
The regional airports mostly serve flights to Moscow and some summer charter flights to Bulgaria, Turkey and Croatia.
Kiev's newly-renovated Boryspil airport serves the bulk of international flights offered by Ukrainian carriers and major western and central European airlines.
The other two major airports served by western European carriers are at the eastern industrial city of Dnipropetrovsk and at the Black Sea port of Odessa.
